knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Leading Entries of a Matrix

question.:question/problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1\text{st}$ and $2\text{nd}$ rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 9 & 9 & 9 \\ -2 & 9 & 9 & 9 \\ 3 & 9 & 9 & 9 \\ -4 & 9 & 9 & 9\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1\text{st}$ and $2\text{nd}$ rows of $A$ are $1$ and $-2$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 9 & 9 & 9 \\ -2 & 9 & 9 & 9 \\ 3 & 9 & 9 & 9 \\ -4 & 9 & 9 & 9\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $1+(-2)=-1.$
